subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Three Wishes and Fairy Tales
description: A short lesson to help you apply Three Wishes and Fairy Tales.

hook.text: A genie grants three wishes. Goldilocks tries three bowls. The third pig builds with bricks. Three drives stories.

buildup.text: Fairy tales use three as a rhythm: two failures and one success. The pattern trains you to expect a resolution.

discovery.text: Comedians call it the rule of three. Set up, reinforce, surprise. The third beat always breaks the pattern.

twist.text: Two repetitions create a rule. The third either confirms or shatters it. That's why three feels complete.

climax.text: Three isn't just mystical—it's neurological. Our brains recognize patterns at three. Fewer feels random; more bores.

punchline.text: Two set the pattern. Three breaks it.

quiz.question: Why do fairy tales often use the number three?
options: Two failures create a pattern, the third resolves it
